name: Production error masking for server actions

arm-01.note: This codebase has zero Next.js Server Actions ('use server') anywhere -- all mutations go through API routes. Thrown errors surface via `error.message` in ad hoc per-route catch blocks with no dedicated typed-error-to-safe-message convention, and unexpected exceptions fall through to Next's default production error handling. Adequate by accident of Next's defaults, not by a deliberate masking mechanism.

arm-03.note: Also no Server Actions, but lib/result.ts's Result<T,E> type carries a separate `publicMessage` alongside the internal `error` detail on every failure path, and maskError() explicitly returns a generic message in production while showing the real error in development -- a small, deliberate, reusable masking primitive applied broadly across lib/ops, lib/payments, and lib/storefront.

arm-04.note: The only one of the six arms that actually uses real Next.js Server Actions extensively (30 'use server' files driving nearly all admin and account mutations). Each returns a bounded FormState {error, notice} rather than throwing to the client, and lib/core/errors.ts's firstErrorMessage() caps stored error detail to one line/200 chars specifically because a raw error can carry connection strings or row contents that staff-facing logs and cron tables would otherwise expose. This is the arm where the item's literal subject applies most directly, even though the masking discipline is comparable in spirit to arm-03's rather than more advanced.

arm-05.note: Also no Server Actions; API routes return `error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'fallback'` in several places with no dedicated typed-error-to-safe-message mapping layer observed, slightly less structured than the clone cluster's ActionError convention.

arm-06.note: No Server Actions either, but lib/errors.ts (typed NotFoundError/DomainRuleError) + lib/http-errors.ts's mapDomainError()/mapDomainErrorOrThrow() form a deliberate, reusable ladder: known domain errors map to safe messages + correct status codes, an optional `clientMessage` field lets a route show a staff-safe summary while logging the full detail server-side via console.error, and anything unrecognized is rethrown to Next's default (masked) handling. The most deliberately engineered error-masking layer of the batch, even though it targets API routes rather than literal server actions.
